teams.heading: Farrell set to recall Gibson-Park as Sheehan misses Fiji test with concussion
teams.body: Ireland head coach Andy Farrell is set to restore scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park to the starting XV for Saturday's Nations Championship match, with hooker Rónan Kelleher expected to start after captain Dan Sheehan was ruled out of the Fiji fixture with concussion. The expectation is that Farrell avoids sweeping changes, so Fiji, ranked ninth in the world and coached by Jake White, face a largely settled Ireland side. Gibson-Park came off the bench against Argentina, with Craig Casey starting at nine in that win.

lead.why: It is the freshest new item on the shortlist and concerns Fiji's next test, with a selection expectation and a concussion absence.

teams.heading: Jamie George questions Times report of senior players' demands for Borthwick talks
teams.body: A Times report claiming senior players had demanded talks with England head coach Steve Borthwick and senior RFU figures dominated the build-up to Sunday's 45-22 win over Australia, England's most points against the Wallabies. Vice-captain Jamie George questioned both its contents and its timing. World Cup winner Ben Kay calls a fully harmonious changing room naïve and says that in situations like this, "it can actually galvanise the players and bring them together a little bit more." Kay adds that winning makes players forget earlier grumbles.

lead.why: The Williams column and the Feyi-Waboso news are already reported, and this is the only new item in the pack about England's own squad.

teams.heading: Dupont moves to fly-half as France hunt Springboks without Jalibert and Ntamack
teams.body: Antoine Dupont starts at fly-half against South Africa on Friday, with Maxime Lucu at scrum-half, after Matthieu Jalibert, Romain Ntamack, Thomas Ramos and Antoine Hastoy were all absent. Dupont's fly-half experience is limited to a handful of games for Toulouse. South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus says the captain is hard to read: "I don't even know if Dupont's team-mates know exactly what he's going to do next, so he's just really playing on instinct, which is tough to handle."

lead.why: The newest France item on the shortlist: a fly-half selection that changes the test, and not covered in the earlier editions.

teams.heading: Farrell expected to restore Gibson-Park to Ireland's starting XV against Fiji
teams.body: Ireland captain Dan Sheehan is out of Saturday's Fiji game with concussion, the42 reports, and Rónan Kelleher is expected to start at hooker in his place. Ireland scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park, who came off the bench against Argentina while Craig Casey started at nine, looks likely to return to the starting XV alongside Sam Prendergast. James Ryan is also in contention for the second row, and Ireland head coach Andy Farrell may avoid sweeping changes against a Fiji side ranked ninth in the world.

teams.heading: Riccardo Casarin and Antony Italo Miranda join Italy's camp as invited players
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada has added two invitees to the squad training camp in Turin ahead of Saturday's test against Argentina. Riccardo Casarin, a centre at Valorugby, captained Italy U20 in the most recent Six Nations and the Junior Rugby World Cup, and has made an URC debut for Zebre Parma. Antony Italo Miranda, a Mogliano back-rower who was also part of the U20 group last season, joins him, and both are already available to the coaching staff.

teams.heading: Wallabies wary of Scotland's Sione Tuipulotu as Test weekend approaches
teams.body: Australia's caution ahead of the Round five Test is aimed squarely at one Scotland player. Wallabies captain Harry Wilson, speaking after the 45-22 defeat at Twickenham, said: "Scotland are a really good team and we've got to be ready for it." Planet Rugby's opinion column argued Scotland will be a fairer fight for Australia than England was. Scotland, meanwhile, come into the match off a 21-43 loss to New Zealand in Round four.

lead.why: It is the only new Scotland-specific item on the shortlist, and it places a Scotland player at the centre of Australia's preparations.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy weighs Adam Beard recall as Josh Adams may rest
teams.body: Wales head coach Steve Tandy is weighing a pack reshuffle for Saturday's Nations Championship Test against New Zealand. Second-row Adam Beard, who lost his starting place to Ben Carter before the Six Nations, is set to drop to the bench after the Welsh lineout struggled in the 28-21 win over Japan. Josh Adams, who crossed twice against Japan, could be rested, though it is unclear whether that happens this week. Leicester wing Gabriel Hamer-Webb, who has one cap, is touted as the likeliest replacement.

lead.why: It is a fresh Wales selection story that the other shortlist items do not match, and it sits on the Saturday test itself.

teams.heading: Tobías Wade called up after Juan Cruz Mallía's knee sprain in Dublin
teams.body: Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi has added Tobías Wade to the squad after Juan Cruz Mallía sprained a knee against Ireland. The depth behind him is thin: Santiago Carreras is out for the year and Benjamín Elizalde is also injured. Wade, a Zebre Parma fullback who plays his rugby in Italy, is uncapped and featured for the Argentina XV against England A last Friday. He is chasing a first cap, while Mateo Soler is after his second.

lead.why: A fresh selection and injury story about Argentina's own squad, distinct from the Montoya HIA lead already run.

teams.heading: Len Ikitau says Wallabies must connect forwards and backline better against Scotland
teams.body: Australia have conceded 138 points across their three-game losing run, an average of 46 a game, and defence is the first thing to fix before Scotland. Ikitau described the problem as one of connection: "We need to be able to connect well with our forwards and then with our backfield too." Ikitau has had a different midfield partner in three straight matches and will likely reunite with Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii, with Kurtley Beale and Filipo Daugunu the other options.

lead.why: It is the freshest Australia-specific news in the pack, a new defensive diagnosis from Ikitau ahead of Scotland, and the Suaalii and Henry items are already reported.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones concedes Japan must break up the game to beat England
teams.body: Japan head coach Eddie Jones has laid out his route to an upset at Twickenham on Saturday. “We’ll need to be able to break up the game, if we play an orthodox game of rugby, we’re probably going to struggle to beat them,” the Australian said, ahead of a match Japan are expected to enter as overwhelming underdogs. Japan have lost all six previous Test meetings with England, most recently 54-19 on their autumn visit two years ago.

lead.why: It is a NEW item about Japan's own tactics, and its quote gives a different angle from the chaos line already run.

teams.heading: Neil Barnes admits All Blacks must fix maul defence before Wales
teams.body: All Blacks assistant coach Neil Barnes believes the rolling maul rules need no further change, but his team must improve its defence against it. New Zealand conceded two maul tries in the 43-21 win over Scotland at Murrayfield. "There are some finer details that go on in your maul defence that we honestly believe we can be better at," Barnes said. Saturday's Test against Wales is the next chance to fix it.

lead.why: It is a new, New Zealand-specific admission from the assistant coach about a defensive weakness, not a repeat of the Will Jordan injury or the maul-law debate already covered.

teams.heading: Italy captain Giacomo Nicotera flags Springboks' mauls and aerial strength before France
teams.body: Italy coach Gonzalo Quesada admitted his side had faced the world's best team, and captain Giacomo Nicotera said the Springboks were still superior. The mauls South Africa kept launching broke through several times in Turin, and Italy's aerial defence was found wanting. Ruan Nortje was targeted for ten lineout throws, against two for Pieter-Steph du Toit, a workload Nicotera said better aerial defence could have limited. The Springboks face France on Friday at the Stade de France.

lead.why: It is the only new item about South Africa's own play, and the others are either already reported or about another team.
